title: The dimension of a scheme is the supremum of the dimensions of the rings of an affine open cover
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of open subschemes of $X$ with $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, each $U_i$ isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for a commutative ring $A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\dim X$ be the dimension of $X$ [def-pc-dimension] (the supremum of the Krull dimensions of the local rings $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $x\in X$) and $\dim A_i\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ the Krull dimension of the ring $A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then
$$
\dim X=\sup_{i\in I}\dim A_i
$$
in $\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ (an empty $U_i$ has $A_i=0$ and contributes $-\infty$).

source.place: Properties, Lemma 04MU (properties-lemma-dimension, properties.tex line 1233: dim X = sup of the dimensions of the local rings), together with Schemes, Lemma 01HV (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves, schemes.tex line 692: the stalk of the structure sheaf of Spec A at p is A_p) and Algebra, Lemma 00KG (algebra-lemma-dimension-height, algebra.tex line 14353: dim R is the supremum of the heights of its primes); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: For each $i$, use the supplied isomorphism $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ directly. Put $f_i:\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to X$ equal to its inverse followed by the open inclusion. This is an open immersion. For $x\in U_i$, its image $p$ under the isomorphism satisfies $f_i(p)=x$ by the inverse identity. No passage through $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ is required [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

The stalk map of the open immersion $f_i$ is an isomorphism, using the open-immersion stalk-map declaration recorded in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (b). The stalk of $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ at $p$ is the localization of $A_i$ at $p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] (1). Isomorphic rings have equal Krull dimension, since their prime spectra are order-isomorphic [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X,f_i(p)}=\operatorname{ht}p$.

For each $i$, [lem-pc-ring-dimension-supremum-heights] gives $\dim A_i=\sup_{p\in\operatorname{Spec}A_i}\operatorname{ht}p$. In Lean change the indexing type from points of the scheme to PrimeSpectrum before identifying ideal height with order height: the scheme specialization order is the opposite order. The supremum is in WithBot ENat; when the chart is empty both sides are bottom.

Unfold $\dim X=\sup_{x\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-pc-dimension]. For the forward inequality, the cover gives an $i$ and $x\in U_i$. Step 1 gives $p$ with $f_i(p)=x$; step 2 bounds the stalk dimension by the supremum of heights in that chart, which is $\dim A_i$ by step 3 and is bounded by the supremum over $i$. Conversely, for each $i$ and $p$, step 2 identifies $\operatorname{ht}p$ with a stalk dimension of $X$, bounded by $\dim X$. Take the supremum over $p$ using step 3, and then over $i$. Antisymmetry gives the equality.
